evidence.finding: Decision 723 covers three words, all on s337 block 0 line 3: שָׁלֹשׁ, קְדֻשּׁוֹת and מְשַׁלְּשׁוֹת, in 'כִּתּוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ מְשַׁלְּשׁוֹת'. Each records 'Explicit user enlarged-source adjudication'. No Tetragrammaton is involved.

The recorded convention reads: 'Source lacks separately printed holam; encode logical holam U+05B9 and shin dot separately per user and specs/BIRNBAUM_FROM_SCAN.md combined-dot rule lines331–342'. Its stated basis is the combined shin-dot/holam rule and nothing broader.

evidence.source: User 723 chat, as quoted in the brief
evidence.finding: 'holam is not printed, but the project conventions say it should be added; yes to both dageshes'. The words 'project conventions' point back to a rule that already existed, the combined-dot rule. The user did not create a new rule. 'Both dageshes' matches 723b/723c. Nothing in the quote mentions the Divine Name.

The rule covers only a holam 'on the letter before a shin, or on the shin itself', where one dot does the work of both marks. It calls itself 'the one place the reading deliberately departs from what the page shows'. Its test (line 352) is whether leaving the mark out changes what the word is. A Tetragrammaton printed without holam has no shin and no merged dot, so the rule's condition is never met. Printing the Name without holam is also a recognised convention in its own right, and leaving the mark out does not turn it into a different word.

Line 24-25: 'Do not generalize a confirmed mark from one occurrence to other occurrences of the same word.' Generalizing it to a different word class is a further step that this rule rules out a fortiori. Lines 49-54: legitimate alternatives stay as ordinary source text, not sic/corr. Lines 55-57: an editorial normalization needs an explicit authorization and record. None exists for the Tetragrammaton.

The claim says 'The existing user723 holam-supply convention for the literal Tetragrammaton applies here too'. No record cites a source for it, and it contradicts both the 723 record and the scope of the combined-dot rule. It is an inference written by an assistant, not user authority. Any later AI review that accepted this premise is not new approval either.
